atoms.text: King Snowy wants to tell you about his home. Will you learn about the North Pole with him?

instruction.text: King Snowy wants to find his home on a world map. Can you point out the North Pole to him?

feedback.end: The North Pole is the most northern point on Earth. It is located in the Arctic Ocean.

instruction.text: The North Pole is very cold. Select the images of things you might see there.
Find the polar bear in this image to tell King Snowy a fun fact about the North Pole.

feedback.end: The North Pole isn’t actually on any proper piece of land. It’s on some ice floating around in the ocean!

instruction.text: At the North Pole, there is constant sunlight in summer and constant darkness in winter. Answer King Snowy’s questions.

atoms.a: “If it is summer right now, what can I see in the sky?”
atoms.sound: ssml:<voice voiceLang='en' voice='m10'>If it is summer right now, what can I see in the sky?</voice>

hint.text: At the North Pole, the sun stays in the sky for six months. Then it sets and can’t be seen again for another six months.

atoms.a: “Can I see the sunrise and sunset every day?”
atoms.sound: ssml:<voice voiceLang='en' voice='m10'>Can I see the sunrise and sunset every day?</voice>
